## One-Sentence Summary

A lightweight, privacy-first tool that generates a verifiable fingerprint of a file and anchors it to a public, time-stamped ledger so anyone can prove originality and authenticity.

## Problem

The creators describe a digital landscape saturated with deepfakes, fake screenshots, copied artwork, and altered media, where "anyone can post anything," making it increasingly difficult to establish what's original or real. They frame the central question as how people can credibly prove ownership or first possession of digital work amid pervasive manipulation and duplication.

## Solution / Product Overview

The product creates a digital fingerprint of a user's file and records proof of that fingerprint on a public, time-stamped ledger. The approach is presented as secure and privacy-preserving: users do not upload the actual file; instead, a compact fingerprint is used as a durable evidence marker. The creators position this as a quiet safeguard for digital truth that everyday people, as well as professionals, can rely on.

## Key Features & Capabilities

-   File fingerprinting: produces a unique hash of a file for proof of originality.

-   Public, time-stamped anchoring: writes proof to a ledger that can be independently checked.

-   Privacy-first design: only hashed fingerprints are stored, not the underlying files.

-   Lightweight implementation: designed to be efficient and resource-conscious.

-   Security emphasis: presented as "lightweight, secure, and built for the future."

## Target Users & Use Cases

The campaign calls out artists, small businesses, journalists, and anyone who wants to prove "I had this first." Primary uses include establishing authorship, deterring copycats, and documenting the creation time of digital assets.

## Development Status

The "core protocol already works," and an early form is live privately. The team is seeking to build a cleaner public interface and supporting infrastructure so the tool is usable by a broader audience.

## Roadmap & Delivery Plan

Planned steps include hiring a developer and a designer to build a smoother public interface; polishing usability; and layering in infrastructure for scale. The team references a January beta target and says cushion time has been built into the schedule.

## Why Crowdfunding / Use of Funds

Funds will support building a public-facing site and the underlying infrastructure, along with the hiring needed to deliver a refined interface and broaden access.

## Risks & Challenges

The main risk is talent acquisition: delays in hiring or extended timelines could push back the January beta. Mitigations include existing architecture, a lean scope, added schedule buffer, and a commitment to communicate changes clearly.

## Team & Partnerships

The effort is led by engineers who emphasize building for everyday creators in their lives. All architecture and content are created and reviewed by a human team.

## Technical Details

Only hashed fingerprints are stored, dramatically reducing storage and compute compared with systems that store full files or rely on energy-intensive consensus mechanisms. The goal is long-term security and transparency with minimal environmental impact.

## Support & Post-Launch Plans

The team promises clear communication with backers if plans change and notes limited, supportive use of AI tools for coding and documentation; they are not building AI technology nor using AI to generate creative assets.

## One-Sentence Summary

A lightweight, privacy-first tool that generates a verifiable fingerprint of a file and anchors it to a public, time-stamped ledger so anyone can prove originality and authenticity.

## Problem

The creators describe a digital landscape saturated with deepfakes, fake screenshots, copied artwork, and altered media, where "anyone can post anything," making it increasingly difficult to establish what's original or real. They frame the central question as how people can credibly prove ownership or first possession of digital work amid pervasive manipulation and duplication.

## Solution / Product Overview

The product creates a digital fingerprint of a user's file and records proof of that fingerprint on a public, time-stamped ledger. The approach is presented as secure and privacy-preserving: users do not upload the actual file; instead, a compact fingerprint is used as a durable evidence marker. The creators position this as a quiet safeguard for digital truth that everyday people, as well as professionals, can rely on.

## Key Features & Capabilities

-   File fingerprinting: produces a unique hash of a file for proof of originality.
-   Public, time-stamped anchoring: writes proof to a ledger that can be independently checked.
-   Privacy-first design: only hashed fingerprints are stored, not the underlying files.
-   Lightweight implementation: designed to be efficient and resource-conscious.
-   Security emphasis: presented as "lightweight, secure, and built for the future."

## Target Users & Use Cases

The campaign calls out artists, small businesses, journalists, and anyone who wants to prove "I had this first." Primary uses include establishing authorship, deterring copycats, and documenting the creation time of digital assets. To focus the initial beta launch, the team proposes concentrating development and marketing efforts on a specific, narrow user segment. The proposed initial target is digital illustrators who primarily share their work on a single, major social media platform.

## Development Status

The "core protocol already works," and an early form is live privately. The team is seeking to build a cleaner public interface and supporting infrastructure so the tool is usable by a broader audience.

## Roadmap & Delivery Plan

Planned steps include hiring a developer and a designer to build a smoother public interface; polishing usability; and layering in infrastructure for scale. The team references a January beta target and says cushion time has been built into the schedule. As part of this plan, the team proposes to tailor the initial beta interface and user experience specifically for the needs and workflows of the proposed target segment of digital illustrators.

## Why Crowdfunding / Use of Funds

Funds will support building a public-facing site and the underlying infrastructure, along with the hiring needed to deliver a refined interface and broaden access. This includes proposed work to adapt the initial product for the specific segment.

## Risks & Challenges

The main risk is talent acquisition: delays in hiring or extended timelines could push back the January beta. Mitigations include existing architecture, a lean scope, added schedule buffer, and a commitment to communicate changes clearly. Focusing on a narrow initial segment is a proposed strategy to manage scope and accelerate learning.

## Team & Partnerships

The effort is led by engineers who emphasize building for everyday creators in their lives. All architecture and content are created and reviewed by a human team.

## Technical Details

Only hashed fingerprints are stored, dramatically reducing storage and compute compared with systems that store full files or rely on energy-intensive consensus mechanisms. The goal is long-term security and transparency with minimal environmental impact.

## Support & Post-Launch Plans

The team promises clear communication with backers if plans change and notes limited, supportive use of AI tools for coding and documentation; they are not building AI technology nor using AI to generate creative assets. The plan is to gather feedback from the initial, focused user segment to inform broader development.

## One-Sentence Summary

A lightweight, privacy-first tool that generates a verifiable fingerprint of a file and anchors it to a public, time-stamped ledger so anyone can prove originality and authenticity.

## Problem

The creators describe a digital landscape saturated with deepfakes, fake screenshots, copied artwork, and altered media, where "anyone can post anything," making it increasingly difficult to establish what's original or real. They frame the central question as how people can credibly prove ownership or first possession of digital work amid pervasive manipulation and duplication.

## Solution / Product Overview

The product creates a digital fingerprint of a user's file and records proof of that fingerprint on a public, time-stamped ledger. The approach is presented as secure and privacy-preserving: users do not upload the actual file; instead, a compact fingerprint is used as a durable evidence marker. The creators position this as a quiet safeguard for digital truth that everyday people, as well as professionals, can rely on.

## Key Features & Capabilities

-   File fingerprinting: produces a unique hash of a file for proof of originality.
-   Public, time-stamped anchoring: writes proof to a ledger that can be independently checked.
-   Privacy-first design: only hashed fingerprints are stored, not the underlying files.
-   Lightweight implementation: designed to be efficient and resource-conscious.
-   Security emphasis: presented as "lightweight, secure, and built for the future."

## Target Users & Use Cases

The campaign calls out artists, small businesses, journalists, and anyone who wants to prove "I had this first." Primary uses include establishing authorship, deterring copycats, and documenting the creation time of digital assets. To focus the initial beta launch, the team proposes concentrating development and marketing efforts on a specific, narrow user segment. The proposed initial target is digital illustrators who primarily share their work on a single, major social media platform.

## Development Status

The "core protocol already works," and an early form is live privately. The team is seeking to build a cleaner public interface and supporting infrastructure so the tool is usable by a broader audience.

## Roadmap & Delivery Plan

Planned steps include hiring a developer and a designer to build a smoother public interface; polishing usability; and layering in infrastructure for scale. The team references a January beta target and says cushion time has been built into the schedule. As part of this plan, the team proposes to tailor the initial beta interface and user experience specifically for the needs and workflows of the proposed target segment of digital illustrators. To inform this tailoring, the team proposes a small-scale, planned test with a handful of digital illustrators from the target platform to gather initial workflow feedback before the beta.

## Why Crowdfunding / Use of Funds

Funds will support building a public-facing site and the underlying infrastructure, along with the hiring needed to deliver a refined interface and broaden access. This includes proposed work to adapt the initial product for the specific segment and to conduct the proposed small-scale test.

## Risks & Challenges

The main risk is talent acquisition: delays in hiring or extended timelines could push back the January beta. Mitigations include existing architecture, a lean scope, added schedule buffer, and a commitment to communicate changes clearly. Focusing on a narrow initial segment is a proposed strategy to manage scope and accelerate learning.

## Team & Partnerships

The effort is led by engineers who emphasize building for everyday creators in their lives. All architecture and content are created and reviewed by a human team.

## Technical Details

Only hashed fingerprints are stored, dramatically reducing storage and compute compared with systems that store full files or rely on energy-intensive consensus mechanisms. The goal is long-term security and transparency with minimal environmental impact.

## Support & Post-Launch Plans

The team promises clear communication with backers if plans change and notes limited, supportive use of AI tools for coding and documentation; they are not building AI technology nor using AI to generate creative assets. The plan is to gather feedback from the initial, focused user segment, informed by the proposed small-scale test, to inform broader development.

A lightweight, privacy-first tool that generates a verifiable fingerprint of a file and anchors it to a public, time-stamped ledger so anyone can prove originality and authenticity.

## Problem

The creators describe a digital landscape saturated with deepfakes, fake screenshots, copied artwork, and altered media, where "anyone can post anything," making it increasingly difficult to establish what's original or real. They frame the central question as how people can credibly prove ownership or first possession of digital work amid pervasive manipulation and duplication.

## Solution / Product Overview

The product creates a digital fingerprint of a user's file and records proof of that fingerprint on a public, time-stamped ledger. The approach is presented as secure and privacy-preserving: users do not upload the actual file; instead, a compact fingerprint is used as a durable evidence marker. The creators position this as a quiet safeguard for digital truth that everyday people, as well as professionals, can rely on.

## Key Features & Capabilities

-   File fingerprinting: produces a unique hash of a file for proof of originality.
-   Public, time-stamped anchoring: writes proof to a ledger that can be independently checked.
-   Privacy-first design: only hashed fingerprints are stored, not the underlying files.
-   Lightweight implementation: designed to be efficient and resource-conscious.
-   Security emphasis: presented as "lightweight, secure, and built for the future."

## Target Users & Use Cases

The campaign calls out artists, small businesses, journalists, and anyone who wants to prove "I had this first." Primary uses include establishing authorship, deterring copycats, and documenting the creation time of digital assets. To focus the initial beta launch, the team proposes concentrating development and marketing efforts on a specific, narrow user segment. The proposed initial target is digital illustrators who primarily share their work on a single, major social media platform.

## Development Status

The "core protocol already works," and an early form is live privately. The team is seeking to build a cleaner public interface and supporting infrastructure so the tool is usable by a broader audience.

## Roadmap & Delivery Plan

Planned steps include hiring a developer and a designer to build a smoother public interface; polishing usability; and layering in infrastructure for scale. The team references a January beta target and says cushion time has been built into the schedule. As part of this plan, the team proposes to tailor the initial beta interface and user experience specifically for the needs and workflows of the proposed target segment of digital illustrators. To inform this tailoring, the team proposes a small-scale, planned test with a handful of digital illustrators from the target platform to gather initial workflow feedback before the beta. Furthermore, the team proposes a planned, small-scale public demonstration of the technology's verification capability using a sample file to be conducted during the crowdfunding campaign to build trust.

## Why Crowdfunding / Use of Funds

Funds will support building a public-facing site and the underlying infrastructure, along with the hiring needed to deliver a refined interface and broaden access. This includes proposed work to adapt the initial product for the specific segment, to conduct the proposed small-scale test, and to execute the proposed public demonstration.

## Risks & Challenges

The main risk is talent acquisition: delays in hiring or extended timelines could push back the January beta. Mitigations include existing architecture, a lean scope, added schedule buffer, and a commitment to communicate changes clearly. Focusing on a narrow initial segment is a proposed strategy to manage scope and accelerate learning.

## Team & Partnerships

The effort is led by engineers who emphasize building for everyday creators in their lives. All architecture and content are created and reviewed by a human team.

## Technical Details

Only hashed fingerprints are stored, dramatically reducing storage and compute compared with systems that store full files or rely on energy-intensive consensus mechanisms. The goal is long-term security and transparency with minimal environmental impact.

## Support & Post-Launch Plans

The team promises clear communication with backers if plans change and notes limited, supportive use of AI tools for coding and documentation; they are not building AI technology nor using AI to generate creative assets. The plan is to gather feedback from the initial, focused user segment, informed by the proposed small-scale test, to inform broader development.

## One-Sentence Summary

A lightweight, privacy-first tool that generates a verifiable fingerprint of a file and anchors it to a public, time-stamped ledger so anyone can prove originality and authenticity.

## Problem

The creators describe a digital landscape saturated with deepfakes, fake screenshots, copied artwork, and altered media, where "anyone can post anything," making it increasingly difficult to establish what's original or real. They frame the central question as how people can credibly prove ownership or first possession of digital work amid pervasive manipulation and duplication.

## Solution / Product Overview

The product creates a digital fingerprint of a user's file and records proof of that fingerprint on a public, time-stamped ledger. The approach is presented as secure and privacy-preserving: users do not upload the actual file; instead, a compact fingerprint is used as a durable evidence marker. The creators position this as a quiet safeguard for digital truth that everyday people, as well as professionals, can rely on.

## Key Features & Capabilities

-   File fingerprinting: produces a unique hash of a file for proof of originality.
-   Public, time-stamped anchoring: writes proof to a ledger that can be independently checked.
-   Privacy-first design: only hashed fingerprints are stored, not the underlying files.
-   Lightweight implementation: designed to be efficient and resource-conscious.
-   Security emphasis: presented as "lightweight, secure, and built for the future."

## Target Users & Use Cases

The campaign calls out artists, small businesses, journalists, and anyone who wants to prove "I had this first." Primary uses include establishing authorship, deterring copycats, and documenting the creation time of digital assets. To focus the initial beta launch, the team proposes concentrating development and marketing efforts on a specific, narrow user segment. The proposed initial target is digital illustrators who primarily share their work on a single, major social media platform.

## Development Status

The "core protocol already works," and an early form is live privately. The team is seeking to build a cleaner public interface and supporting infrastructure so the tool is usable by a broader audience.

## Roadmap & Delivery Plan

Planned steps include hiring a developer and a designer to build a smoother public interface; polishing usability; and layering in infrastructure for scale. The team references a January beta target and says cushion time has been built into the schedule. As part of this plan, the team proposes to tailor the initial beta interface and user experience specifically for the needs and workflows of the proposed target segment of digital illustrators. To inform this tailoring, the team proposes a small-scale, planned test with a handful of digital illustrators from the target platform to gather initial workflow feedback before the beta. Furthermore, the team proposes a planned, small-scale public demonstration of the technology's verification capability using a sample file to be conducted during the crowdfunding campaign to build trust.

## Why Crowdfunding / Use of Funds

Funds will support building a public-facing site and the underlying infrastructure, along with the hiring needed to deliver a refined interface and broaden access. This includes proposed work to adapt the initial product for the specific segment, to conduct the proposed small-scale test, and to execute the proposed public demonstration.

## Risks & Challenges

The main risk is talent acquisition: delays in hiring or extended timelines could push back the January beta. Mitigations include existing architecture, a lean scope, added schedule buffer, and a commitment to communicate changes clearly. Focusing on a narrow initial segment is a proposed strategy to manage scope and accelerate learning.

## Team & Partnerships

The effort is led by engineers who emphasize building for everyday creators in their lives. All architecture and content are created and reviewed by a human team.

## Technical Details

Only hashed fingerprints are stored, dramatically reducing storage and compute compared with systems that store full files or rely on energy-intensive consensus mechanisms. The goal is long-term security and transparency with minimal environmental impact.

## Support & Post-Launch Plans

The team promises clear communication with backers if plans change and notes limited, supportive use of AI tools for coding and documentation; they are not building AI technology nor using AI to generate creative assets. The plan is to gather feedback from the initial, focused user segment, informed by the proposed small-scale test, to inform broader development.

## One-Sentence Summary

A lightweight, privacy-first tool that generates a verifiable fingerprint of a file and anchors it to a public, time-stamped ledger so anyone can prove originality and authenticity.

## Problem

The creators describe a digital landscape saturated with deepfakes, fake screenshots, copied artwork, and altered media, where "anyone can post anything," making it increasingly difficult to establish what's original or real. They frame the central question as how people can credibly prove ownership or first possession of digital work amid pervasive manipulation and duplication.

## Solution / Product Overview

The product creates a digital fingerprint of a user's file and records proof of that fingerprint on a public, time-stamped ledger. The approach is presented as secure and privacy-preserving: users do not upload the actual file; instead, a compact fingerprint is used as a durable evidence marker. The creators position this as a quiet safeguard for digital truth that everyday people, as well as professionals, can rely on.

## Key Features & Capabilities

- File fingerprinting: produces a unique hash of a file for proof of originality.
- Public, time-stamped anchoring: writes proof to a ledger that can be independently checked.
- Privacy-first design: only hashed fingerprints are stored, not the underlying files.
- Lightweight implementation: designed to be efficient and resource-conscious.
- Security emphasis: presented as "lightweight, secure, and built for the future."

## Target Users & Use Cases

The campaign calls out artists, small businesses, journalists, and anyone who wants to prove "I had this first." Primary uses include establishing authorship, deterring copycats, and documenting the creation time of digital assets. To focus the initial beta launch, the team proposes concentrating development and marketing efforts on a specific, narrow user segment. The proposed initial target is digital illustrators who primarily share their work on a single, major social media platform.

## Development Status

The "core protocol already works," and an early form is live privately. The team is seeking to build a cleaner public interface and supporting infrastructure so the tool is usable by a broader audience.

## Roadmap & Delivery Plan

Planned steps include hiring a developer and a designer to build a smoother public interface; polishing usability; and layering in infrastructure for scale. ## One-Sentence Summary

A lightweight, privacy-first tool that generates a verifiable fingerprint of a file and anchors it to a public, time-stamped ledger so anyone can prove originality and authenticity.

## Problem

The creators describe a digital landscape saturated with deepfakes, fake screenshots, copied artwork, and altered media, where "anyone can post anything," making it increasingly difficult to establish what's original or real. They frame the central question as how people can credibly prove ownership or first possession of digital work amid pervasive manipulation and duplication.

## Solution / Product Overview

The product creates a digital fingerprint of a user's file and records proof of that fingerprint on a public, time-stamped ledger. The approach is presented as secure and privacy-preserving: users do not upload the actual file; instead, a compact fingerprint is used as a durable evidence marker. The creators position this as a quiet safeguard for digital truth that everyday people, as well as professionals, can rely on.

## Key Features & Capabilities

- File fingerprinting: produces a unique hash of a file for proof of originality.
- Public, time-stamped anchoring: writes proof to a ledger that can be independently checked.
- Privacy-first design: only hashed fingerprints are stored, not the underlying files.
- Lightweight implementation: designed to be efficient and resource-conscious.
- Security emphasis: presented as "lightweight, secure, and built for the future."

## Target Users & Use Cases

The campaign calls out artists, small businesses, journalists, and anyone who wants to prove "I had this first." Primary uses include establishing authorship, deterring copycats, and documenting the creation time of digital assets. To focus the initial beta launch, the team proposes concentrating development and marketing efforts on a specific, narrow user segment. The proposed initial target is digital illustrators who primarily share their work on a single, major social media platform.

## Development Status

The "core protocol already works," and an early form is live privately. The team is seeking to build a cleaner public interface and supporting infrastructure so the tool is usable by a broader audience.

## Roadmap & Delivery Plan

Planned steps include hiring a developer and a designer to build a smoother public interface; polishing usability; and layering in infrastructure for scale. The team references a January beta target and says cushion time has been built into the schedule. As part of this plan, the team proposes to tailor the initial beta interface and user experience specifically for the needs and workflows of the proposed target segment of digital illustrators. To inform this tailoring, the team proposes a small-scale, planned test with a handful of digital illustrators from the target platform to gather initial workflow feedback before the beta. Furthermore, the team proposes a planned, small-scale public demonstration of the technology's verification capability using a sample file to be conducted during the crowdfunding campaign to build trust.

## Revenue Model and Sustainability

To address a key backer question about long-term viability, the team is considering a proposed, simple pricing structure. This could take the form of a freemium model, for example, offering a limited number of free verifications per month with a subscription option for higher-volume users. As a hypothetical example to make this tangible, a proposed pricing tier could be '5 free verifications per month, then $5 per month for unlimited.' The final model would be developed based on feedback from the initial beta and the proposed small-scale test.

## Why Crowdfunding / Use of Funds

Funds will support building a public-facing site and the underlying infrastructure, along with the hiring needed to deliver a refined interface and broaden access. This includes proposed work to adapt the initial product for the specific segment, to conduct the proposed small-scale test, and to execute the proposed public demonstration.

## Risks & Challenges

The main risk is talent acquisition: delays in hiring or extended timelines could push back the January beta. Mitigations include existing architecture, a lean scope, added schedule buffer, and a commitment to communicate changes clearly. Focusing on a narrow initial segment is a proposed strategy to manage scope and accelerate learning.

## Team & Partnerships

The effort is led by engineers who emphasize building for everyday creators in their lives. All architecture and content are created and reviewed by a human team.

## Technical Details

Only hashed fingerprints are stored, dramatically reducing storage and compute compared with systems that store full files or rely on energy-intensive consensus mechanisms. The goal is long-term security and transparency with minimal environmental impact.

## Support & Post-Launch Plans

The team promises clear communication with backers if plans change and notes limited, supportive use of AI tools for coding and documentation; they are not building AI technology nor using AI to generate creative assets. The plan is to gather feedback from the initial, focused user segment, informed by the proposed small-scale test, to inform broader development and the proposed pricing model.

## One-Sentence Summary

A lightweight, privacy-first tool that generates a verifiable fingerprint of a file and anchors it to a public, time-stamped ledger so anyone can prove originality and authenticity.

## Problem

The digital landscape is saturated with deepfakes, fake screenshots, copied artwork, and altered media, where "anyone can post anything," making it increasingly difficult to establish what's original or real. The central question is how people can credibly prove ownership or first possession of digital work amid pervasive manipulation and duplication.

## Solution / Product Overview

The product creates a digital fingerprint of a user's file and records proof of that fingerprint on a public, time-stamped ledger. The approach is secure and privacy-preserving: users do not upload the actual file; instead, a compact fingerprint is used as a durable evidence marker. This is positioned as a quiet safeguard for digital truth that everyday people, as well as professionals, can rely on. To make the value proposition more tangible, consider a hypothetical example: a digital illustrator could use the tool to generate a fingerprint of their new artwork file before posting it on the named social platform. Later, if a copy appears elsewhere, the illustrator can publicly prove they had the original file first by showing the time-stamped ledger entry matching their file's fingerprint, without ever revealing the full file.

## Key Features & Capabilities

- File fingerprinting: produces a unique hash of a file for proof of originality.
- Public, time-stamped anchoring: writes proof to a ledger that can be independently checked.
- Privacy-first design: only hashed fingerprints are stored, not the underlying files.
- Lightweight implementation: designed to be efficient and resource-conscious.
- Security emphasis: presented as "lightweight, secure, and built for the future."

## Target Users & Use Cases

The campaign calls out artists, small businesses, journalists, and anyone who wants to prove "I had this first." Primary uses include establishing authorship, deterring copycats, and documenting the creation time of digital assets. To focus the initial beta launch, the team proposes concentrating development and marketing efforts on a specific, narrow user segment. The proposed initial target is digital illustrators who primarily share their work on a single, major social media platform.

## Development Status

The "core protocol already works," and an early form is live privately. The team is seeking to build a cleaner public interface and supporting infrastructure so the tool is usable by a broader audience.

## Roadmap & Delivery Plan

Planned steps include hiring a developer and a designer to build a smoother public interface; polishing usability; and layering in infrastructure for scale. The team references a January beta target and says cushion time has been built into the schedule. As part of this plan, the team proposes to tailor the initial beta interface and user experience specifically for the needs and workflows of the proposed target segment of digital illustrators. To inform this tailoring, the team proposes a small-scale, planned test with a handful of digital illustrators from the target platform to gather initial workflow feedback before the beta. Furthermore, the team proposes a planned, small-scale public demonstration of the technology's verification capability using a sample file to be conducted during the crowdfunding campaign to build trust.

## Revenue Model and Sustainability

To address a key backer question about long-term viability, the team is considering a proposed, simple pricing structure. This could take the form of a freemium model, for example, offering a limited number of free verifications per month with a subscription option for higher-volume users. As a hypothetical example to make this tangible, a proposed pricing tier could be '5 free verifications per month, then $5 per month for unlimited.' The final model would be developed based on feedback from the initial beta and the proposed small-scale test.

## Why Crowdfunding / Use of Funds

Funds will support building a public-facing site and the underlying infrastructure, along with the hiring needed to deliver a refined interface and broaden access. This includes proposed work to adapt the initial product for the specific segment, to conduct the proposed small-scale test, and to execute the proposed public demonstration.

## Risks & Challenges

The main risk is talent acquisition: delays in hiring or extended timelines could push back the January beta. Mitigations include existing architecture, a lean scope, added schedule buffer, and a commitment to communicate changes clearly. Focusing on a narrow initial segment is a proposed strategy to manage scope and accelerate learning.

## Team & Partnerships

The effort is led by engineers who emphasize building for everyday creators in their lives. All architecture and content are created and reviewed by a human team.

## Technical Details

Only hashed fingerprints are stored, dramatically reducing storage and compute compared with systems that store full files or rely on energy-intensive consensus mechanisms. The goal is long-term security and transparency with minimal environmental impact.

## Support & Post-Launch Plans

The team promises clear communication with backers if plans change and notes limited, supportive use of AI tools for coding and documentation; they are not building AI technology nor using AI to generate creative assets. The plan is to gather feedback from the initial, focused user segment, informed by the proposed small-scale test, to inform broader development and the proposed pricing model.

## One-Sentence Summary

A lightweight, privacy-first tool that generates a verifiable fingerprint of a file and anchors it to a public, time-stamped ledger so anyone can prove originality and authenticity.

## Problem

The digital landscape is saturated with deepfakes, fake screenshots, copied artwork, and altered media, where "anyone can post anything," making it increasingly difficult to establish what's original or real. The central question is how people can credibly prove ownership or first possession of digital work amid pervasive manipulation and duplication.

## Solution / Product Overview

The product creates a digital fingerprint of a user's file and records proof of that fingerprint on a public, time-stamped ledger. The approach is secure and privacy-preserving: users do not upload the actual file; instead, a compact fingerprint is used as a durable evidence marker. This is positioned as a quiet safeguard for digital truth that everyday people, as well as professionals, can rely on. To make the value proposition more tangible, consider a hypothetical example: a digital illustrator could use the tool to generate a fingerprint of their new artwork file before posting it on the named social platform. Later, if a copy appears elsewhere, the illustrator can publicly prove they had the original file first by showing the time-stamped ledger entry matching their file's fingerprint, without ever revealing the full file.

## Key Features & Capabilities

- File fingerprinting: produces a unique hash of a file for proof of originality.
- Public, time-stamped anchoring: writes proof to a ledger that can be independently checked.
- Privacy-first design: only hashed fingerprints are stored, not the underlying files.
- Lightweight implementation: designed to be efficient and resource-conscious.
- Security emphasis: presented as "lightweight, secure, and built for the future."

## Target Users & Use Cases

The campaign calls out artists, small businesses, journalists, and anyone who wants to prove "I had this first." Primary uses include establishing authorship, deterring copycats, and documenting the creation time of digital assets. To focus the initial beta launch, the team proposes concentrating development and marketing efforts on a specific, narrow user segment. The proposed initial target is digital illustrators who primarily share their work on a single, major social media platform.

## Development Status

The "core protocol already works," and an early form is live privately. The team is seeking to build a cleaner public interface and supporting infrastructure so the tool is usable by a broader audience.

## Roadmap & Delivery Plan

Planned steps include hiring a developer and a designer to build a smoother public interface; polishing usability; and layering in infrastructure for scale. The team references a January beta target and says cushion time has been built into the schedule. As part of this plan, the team proposes to tailor the initial beta interface and user experience specifically for the needs and workflows of the proposed target segment of digital illustrators. To inform this tailoring, the team proposes a small-scale, planned test with a handful of digital illustrators from the target platform to gather initial workflow feedback before the beta. Furthermore, the team proposes a planned, small-scale public demonstration of the technology's verification capability using a sample file to be conducted during the crowdfunding campaign to build trust.

## Revenue Model and Sustainability

To address a key backer question about long-term viability, the team is considering a proposed, simple pricing structure. This could take the form of a freemium model, for example, offering a limited number of free verifications per month with a subscription option for higher-volume users. As a hypothetical example to make this tangible, a proposed pricing tier could be '3 free verifications per month, then $5 per month for unlimited.' The final model would be developed based on feedback from the initial beta and the proposed small-scale test.

## Why Crowdfunding / Use of Funds

Funds will support building a public-facing site and the underlying infrastructure, along with the hiring needed to deliver a refined interface and broaden access. This includes proposed work to adapt the initial product for the specific segment, to conduct the proposed small-scale test, and to execute the proposed public demonstration.

## Risks & Challenges

The main risk is talent acquisition: delays in hiring or extended timelines could push back the January beta. Mitigations include existing architecture, a lean scope, added schedule buffer, and a commitment to communicate changes clearly. Focusing on a narrow initial segment is a proposed strategy to manage scope and accelerate learning.

## Team & Partnerships

The effort is led by engineers who emphasize building for everyday creators in their lives. All architecture and content are created and reviewed by a human team.

## Technical Details

Only hashed fingerprints are stored, dramatically reducing storage and compute compared with systems that store full files or rely on energy-intensive consensus mechanisms. The goal is long-term security and transparency with minimal environmental impact.

## Support & Post-Launch Plans

The team promises clear communication with backers if plans change and notes limited, supportive use of AI tools for coding and documentation; they are not building AI technology nor using AI to generate creative assets. The plan is to gather feedback from the initial, focused user segment, informed by the proposed small-scale test, to inform broader development and the proposed pricing model.

## One-Sentence Summary

A lightweight, privacy-first tool that generates a verifiable fingerprint of a file and anchors it to a public, time-stamped ledger so anyone can prove originality and authenticity.

## Problem

The digital landscape is saturated with deepfakes, fake screenshots, copied artwork, and altered media, where "anyone can post anything," making it increasingly difficult to establish what's original or real. The central question is how people can credibly prove ownership or first possession of digital work amid pervasive manipulation and duplication.

## Solution / Product Overview

The product creates a digital fingerprint of a user's file and records proof of that fingerprint on a public, time-stamped ledger. The approach is secure and privacy-preserving: users do not upload the actual file; instead, a compact fingerprint is used as a durable evidence marker. This is positioned as a quiet safeguard for digital truth that everyday people, as well as professionals, can rely on. To make the value proposition more tangible, consider a hypothetical example: a digital illustrator could use the tool to generate a fingerprint of their new artwork file before posting it on the named social platform. Later, if a copy appears elsewhere, the illustrator can publicly prove they had the original file first by showing the time-stamped ledger entry matching their file's fingerprint, without ever revealing the full file.

## Key Features & Capabilities

- File fingerprinting: produces a unique hash of a file for proof of originality.
- Public, time-stamped anchoring: writes proof to a ledger that can be independently checked.
- Privacy-first design: only hashed fingerprints are stored, not the underlying files.
- Lightweight implementation: designed to be efficient and resource-conscious.
- Security emphasis: presented as "lightweight, secure, and built for the future."

## Target Users & Use Cases

The campaign calls out artists, small businesses, journalists, and anyone who wants to prove "I had this first." Primary uses include establishing authorship, deterring copycats, and documenting the creation time of digital assets. To focus the initial beta launch, the team proposes concentrating development and marketing efforts on a specific, narrow user segment. The proposed initial target is digital illustrators who primarily share their work on a single, major social media platform.

## Development Status

The "core protocol already works," and an early form is live privately. The team is seeking to build a cleaner public interface and supporting infrastructure so the tool is usable by a broader audience.

## Roadmap & Delivery Plan

Planned steps include hiring a developer and a designer to build a smoother public interface; polishing usability; and layering in infrastructure for scale. The team references a January beta target and says cushion time has been built into the schedule. As part of this plan, the team proposes to tailor the initial beta interface and user experience specifically for the needs and workflows of the proposed target segment of digital illustrators. To inform this tailoring, the team proposes a small-scale, planned test with a handful of digital illustrators from the target platform to gather initial workflow feedback before the beta. Furthermore, the team proposes a planned, small-scale public demonstration of the technology's verification capability using a sample file to be conducted during the crowdfunding campaign to build trust. To help visualize the solution for this segment, the team proposes to include a mock-up or wireframe screenshot of the proposed beta interface tailored for digital illustrators in the project description.

## Revenue Model and Sustainability

To address a key backer question about long-term viability, the team is considering a proposed, simple pricing structure. This could take the form of a freemium model, for example, offering a limited number of free verifications per month with a subscription option for higher-volume users. As a hypothetical example to make this tangible, a proposed pricing tier could be '5 free verifications per month, then $5 per month for unlimited.' The final model would be developed based on feedback from the initial beta and the proposed small-scale test.

## Why Crowdfunding / Use of Funds

Funds will support building a public-facing site and the underlying infrastructure, along with the hiring needed to deliver a refined interface and broaden access. This includes proposed work to adapt the initial product for the specific segment, to conduct the proposed small-scale test, to execute the proposed public demonstration, and to create the proposed interface mock-up or wireframe.

## Risks & Challenges

The main risk is talent acquisition: delays in hiring or extended timelines could push back the January beta. Mitigations include existing architecture, a lean scope, added schedule buffer, and a commitment to communicate changes clearly. Focusing on a narrow initial segment is a proposed strategy to manage scope and accelerate learning.

## Team & Partnerships

The effort is led by engineers who emphasize building for everyday creators in their lives. All architecture and content are created and reviewed by a human team.

## Technical Details

Only hashed fingerprints are stored, dramatically reducing storage and compute compared with systems that store full files or rely on energy-intensive consensus mechanisms. The goal is long-term security and transparency with minimal environmental impact.

## Support & Post-Launch Plans

The team promises clear communication with backers if plans change and notes limited, supportive use of AI tools for coding and documentation; they are not building AI technology nor using AI to generate creative assets. The plan is to gather feedback from the initial, focused user segment, informed by the proposed small-scale test, to inform broader development and the proposed pricing model.

## One-Sentence Summary

A lightweight, privacy-first tool that generates a verifiable fingerprint of a file and anchors it to a public, time-stamped ledger so anyone can prove originality and authenticity.

## Problem

The digital landscape is saturated with deepfakes, fake screenshots, copied artwork, and altered media, where "anyone can post anything," making it increasingly difficult to establish what's original or real. The central question is how people can credibly prove ownership or first possession of digital work amid pervasive manipulation and duplication.

## Solution / Product Overview

The product creates a digital fingerprint of a user's file and records proof of that fingerprint on a public, time-stamped ledger. The approach is secure and privacy-preserving: users do not upload the actual file; instead, a compact fingerprint is used as a durable evidence marker. This is positioned as a quiet safeguard for digital truth that everyday people, as well as professionals, can rely on. To make the value proposition more tangible, consider a hypothetical example: a digital illustrator could use the tool to generate a fingerprint of their new artwork file before posting it on the named social platform. Later, if a copy appears elsewhere, the illustrator can publicly prove they had the original file first by showing the time-stamped ledger entry matching their file's fingerprint, without ever revealing the full file.

## Key Features & Capabilities

- File fingerprinting: produces a unique hash of a file for proof of originality.
- Public, time-stamped anchoring: writes proof to a ledger that can be independently checked.
- Privacy-first design: only hashed fingerprints are stored, not the underlying files.
- Lightweight implementation: designed to be efficient and resource-conscious.
- Security emphasis: presented as "lightweight, secure, and built for the future."

## Target Users & Use Cases

The campaign calls out artists, small businesses, journalists, and anyone who wants to prove "I had this first." Primary uses include establishing authorship, deterring copycats, and documenting the creation time of digital assets. To focus the initial beta launch, the team proposes concentrating development and marketing efforts on a specific, narrow user segment. The proposed initial target is digital illustrators who primarily share their work on a single, major social media platform.

## Development Status

The "core protocol already works," and an early form is live privately. The team is seeking to build a cleaner public interface and supporting infrastructure so the tool is usable by a broader audience.

## Roadmap & Delivery Plan

Planned steps include hiring a developer and a designer to build a smoother public interface; polishing usability; and layering in infrastructure for scale. The team references a January beta target and says cushion time has been built into the schedule. As part of this plan, the team proposes to tailor the initial beta interface and user experience specifically for the needs and workflows of the proposed target segment of digital illustrators. To inform this tailoring, the team proposes a small-scale, planned test with a handful of digital illustrators from the target platform to gather initial workflow feedback before the beta, planned for the month following successful funding. Furthermore, the team proposes a planned, small-scale public demonstration of the technology's verification capability using a sample file to be conducted during the crowdfunding campaign to build trust, planned for the third week of the campaign. To help visualize the solution for this segment, the team proposes to include a mock-up or wireframe screenshot of the proposed beta interface tailored for digital illustrators in the project description.

## Revenue Model and Sustainability

To address a key backer question about long-term viability, the team is considering a proposed, simple pricing structure. This could take the form of a freemium model, for example, offering a limited number of free verifications per month with a subscription option for higher-volume users. As a hypothetical example to make this tangible, a proposed pricing tier could be '5 free verifications per month, then $5 per month for unlimited.' The final model would be developed based on feedback from the initial beta and the proposed small-scale test.

## Why Crowdfunding / Use of Funds

Funds will support building a public-facing site and the underlying infrastructure, along with the hiring needed to deliver a refined interface and broaden access. This includes proposed work to adapt the initial product for the specific segment, to conduct the proposed small-scale test, to execute the proposed public demonstration, and to create the proposed interface mock-up or wireframe.

## Risks & Challenges

The main risk is talent acquisition: delays in hiring or extended timelines could push back the January beta. Mitigations include existing architecture, a lean scope, added schedule buffer, and a commitment to communicate changes clearly. Focusing on a narrow initial segment is a proposed strategy to manage scope and accelerate learning.

## Team & Partnerships

The effort is led by engineers who emphasize building for everyday creators in their lives. All architecture and content are created and reviewed by a human team.

## Technical Details

Only hashed fingerprints are stored, dramatically reducing storage and compute compared with systems that store full files or rely on energy-intensive consensus mechanisms. The goal is long-term security and transparency with minimal environmental impact.

## Support & Post-Launch Plans

The team promises clear communication with backers if plans change and notes limited, supportive use of AI tools for coding and documentation; they are not building AI technology nor using AI to generate creative assets. The plan is to gather feedback from the initial, focused user segment, informed by the proposed small-scale test, to inform broader development and the proposed pricing model.

## One-Sentence Summary

A lightweight, privacy-first tool that generates a verifiable fingerprint of a file and anchors it to a public, time-stamped ledger so anyone can prove originality and authenticity.

## Problem

The digital landscape is saturated with deepfakes, fake screenshots, copied artwork, and altered media, where "anyone can post anything," making it increasingly difficult to establish what's original or real. The central question is how people can credibly prove ownership or first possession of digital work amid pervasive manipulation and duplication.

## Solution / Product Overview

The product creates a digital fingerprint of a user's file and records proof of that fingerprint on a public, time-stamped ledger. The approach is secure and privacy-preserving: users do not upload the actual file; instead, a compact fingerprint is used as a durable evidence marker. This is positioned as a quiet safeguard for digital truth that everyday people, as well as professionals, can rely on. To make the value proposition more tangible, consider a hypothetical example: a digital illustrator could use the tool to generate a fingerprint of their new artwork file before posting it on the named social platform. Later, if a copy appears elsewhere, the illustrator can publicly prove they had the original file first by showing the time-stamped ledger entry matching their file's fingerprint, without ever revealing the full file.

## Key Features & Capabilities

- File fingerprinting: produces a unique hash of a file for proof of originality.
- Public, time-stamped anchoring: writes proof to a ledger that can be independently checked.
- Privacy-first design: only hashed fingerprints are stored, not the underlying files.
- Lightweight implementation: designed to be efficient and resource-conscious.
- Security emphasis: presented as "lightweight, secure, and built for the future."

## Target Users & Use Cases

The campaign calls out artists, small businesses, journalists, and anyone who wants to prove "I had this first." Primary uses include establishing authorship, deterring copycats, and documenting the creation time of digital assets. To focus the initial beta launch, the team proposes concentrating development and marketing efforts on a specific, narrow user segment. The proposed initial target is digital illustrators who primarily share their work on a single, major social media platform.

## Development Status

The "core protocol already works," and an early form is live privately. The team is seeking to build a cleaner public interface and supporting infrastructure so the tool is usable by a broader audience.

## Roadmap & Delivery Plan

Planned steps include hiring a developer and a designer to build a smoother public interface; polishing usability; and layering in infrastructure for scale. The team references a January beta target and says cushion time has been built into the schedule. As part of this plan, the team proposes to tailor the initial beta interface and user experience specifically for the needs and workflows of the proposed target segment of digital illustrators. To inform this tailoring, the team proposes a small-scale, planned test with a handful of digital illustrators from the target platform to gather initial workflow feedback before the beta, planned for the month following successful funding. This test is proposed to involve a clear, simple metric of 5 test users to show structured planning and manageability. Furthermore, the team proposes a planned, small-scale public demonstration of the technology's verification capability using a sample file to be conducted during the crowdfunding campaign to build trust, planned for the third week of the campaign. To help visualize the solution for this segment, the team proposes to include a mock-up or wireframe screenshot of the proposed beta interface tailored for digital illustrators in the project description.

## Revenue Model and Sustainability

To address a key backer question about long-term viability, the team is considering a proposed, simple pricing structure. This could take the form of a freemium model, for example, offering a limited number of free verifications per month with a subscription option for higher-volume users. As a hypothetical example to make this tangible, a proposed pricing tier could be '5 free verifications per month, then $5 per month for unlimited.' The final model would be developed based on feedback from the initial beta and the proposed small-scale test.

## Why Crowdfunding / Use of Funds

Funds will support building a public-facing site and the underlying infrastructure, along with the hiring needed to deliver a refined interface and broaden access. This includes proposed work to adapt the initial product for the specific segment, to conduct the proposed small-scale test, to execute the proposed public demonstration, and to create the proposed interface mock-up or wireframe.

## Risks & Challenges

The main risk is talent acquisition: delays in hiring or extended timelines could push back the January beta. Mitigations include existing architecture, a lean scope, added schedule buffer, and a commitment to communicate changes clearly. Focusing on a narrow initial segment is a proposed strategy to manage scope and accelerate learning.

## Team & Partnerships

The effort is led by engineers who emphasize building for everyday creators in their lives. All architecture and content are created and reviewed by a human team.

## Technical Details

Only hashed fingerprints are stored, dramatically reducing storage and compute compared with systems that store full files or rely on energy-intensive consensus mechanisms. The goal is long-term security and transparency with minimal environmental impact.

## Support & Post-Launch Plans

The team promises clear communication with backers if plans change and notes limited, supportive use of AI tools for coding and documentation; they are not building AI technology nor using AI to generate creative assets. The plan is to gather feedback from the initial, focused user segment, informed by the proposed small-scale test, to inform broader development and the proposed pricing model.

## One-Sentence Summary

A lightweight, privacy-first tool that generates a verifiable fingerprint of a file and anchors it to a public, time-stamped ledger so anyone can prove originality and authenticity.

## Problem
The digital landscape is saturated with deepfakes, fake screenshots, copied artwork, and altered media, where "anyone can post anything," making it increasingly difficult to establish what's original or real. The central question is how people can credibly prove ownership or first possession of digital work amid pervasive manipulation and duplication.

## Solution / Product Overview
The product creates a digital fingerprint of a user's file and records proof of that fingerprint on a public, time-stamped ledger. The approach is secure and privacy-preserving: users do not upload the actual file; instead, a compact fingerprint is used as a durable evidence marker. This is positioned as a quiet safeguard for digital truth that everyday people, as well as professionals, can rely on. To make the value proposition more tangible, consider a hypothetical example: a digital illustrator could use the tool to generate a fingerprint of their new artwork file before posting it on the named social platform. Later, if a copy appears elsewhere, the illustrator can publicly prove they had the original file first by showing the time-stamped ledger entry matching their file's fingerprint, without ever revealing the full file.

## Key Features & Capabilities
- File fingerprinting: produces a unique hash of a file for proof of originality.
- Public, time-stamped anchoring: writes proof to a ledger that can be independently checked.
- Privacy-first design: only hashed fingerprints are stored, not the underlying files.
- Lightweight implementation: designed to be efficient and resource-conscious.
- Security emphasis: presented as "lightweight, secure, and built for the future."

## Target Users & Use Cases
The campaign calls out artists, small businesses, journalists, and anyone who wants to prove "I had this first." Primary uses include establishing authorship, deterring copycats, and documenting the creation time of digital assets. To focus the initial beta launch, the team proposes concentrating development and marketing efforts on a specific, narrow user segment. The proposed initial target is digital illustrators who primarily share their work on a single, major social media platform.

## Development Status
The "core protocol already works," and an early form is live privately. The team is seeking to build a cleaner public interface and supporting infrastructure so the tool is usable by a broader audience.

## Roadmap & Delivery Plan
Planned steps include hiring a developer and a designer to build a smoother public interface; polishing usability; and layering in infrastructure for scale. The team references a January beta target and says cushion time has been built into the schedule. As part of this plan, the team proposes to tailor the initial beta interface and user experience specifically for the needs and workflows of the proposed target segment of digital illustrators. To inform this tailoring, the team proposes a small-scale, planned test with a handful of digital illustrators from the target platform to gather initial workflow feedback before the beta, planned for the month following successful funding. This test is proposed to involve a clear, simple metric of 5 test users to show structured planning and manageability. A proposed, clear metric for the success of this test is the percentage of test users who successfully completed the fingerprinting workflow without assistance. Furthermore, the team proposes a planned, small-scale public demonstration of the technology's verification capability using a sample file to be conducted during the crowdfunding campaign to build trust, planned for the third week of the campaign. To help visualize the solution for this segment, the team proposes to include a mock-up or wireframe screenshot of the proposed beta interface tailored for digital illustrators in the project description.

## Revenue Model and Sustainability
To address a key backer question about long-term viability, the team is considering a proposed, simple pricing structure. This could take the form of a freemium model, for example, offering a limited number of free verifications per month with a subscription option for higher-volume users. As a hypothetical example to make this tangible, a proposed pricing tier could be '5 free verifications per month, then $5 per month for unlimited.' The final model would be developed based on feedback from the initial beta and the proposed small-scale test.

## One-Sentence Summary

A lightweight, privacy-first tool that generates a verifiable fingerprint of a file and anchors it to a public, time-stamped ledger so anyone can prove originality and authenticity.

## Problem
The digital landscape is saturated with deepfakes, fake screenshots, copied artwork, and altered media, where "anyone can post anything," making it increasingly difficult to establish what's original or real. The central question is how people can credibly prove ownership or first possession of digital work amid pervasive manipulation and duplication.

## Solution / Product Overview
The product creates a digital fingerprint of a user's file and records proof of that fingerprint on a public, time-stamped ledger. The approach is secure and privacy-preserving: users do not upload the actual file; instead, a compact fingerprint is used as a durable evidence marker. This is positioned as a quiet safeguard for digital truth that everyday people, as well as professionals, can rely on. To make the value proposition more tangible, consider a hypothetical example: a digital illustrator could use the tool to generate a fingerprint of their new artwork file before posting it on the named social platform. Later, if a copy appears elsewhere, the illustrator can publicly prove they had the original file first by showing the time-stamped ledger entry matching their file's fingerprint, without ever revealing the full file.

## Key Features & Capabilities
- File fingerprinting: produces a unique hash of a file for proof of originality.
- Public, time-stamped anchoring: writes proof to a ledger that can be independently checked.
- Privacy-first design: only hashed fingerprints are stored, not the underlying files.
- Lightweight implementation: designed to be efficient and resource-conscious.
- Security emphasis: presented as "lightweight, secure, and built for the future."

## Target Users & Use Cases
The campaign calls out artists, small businesses, journalists, and anyone who wants to prove "I had this first." Primary uses include establishing authorship, deterring copycats, and documenting the creation time of digital assets. To focus the initial beta launch, the team proposes concentrating development and marketing efforts on a specific, narrow user segment. The proposed initial target is digital illustrators who primarily share their work on a single, major social media platform.

## Development Status
The "core protocol already works," and an early form is live privately. The team is seeking to build a cleaner public interface and supporting infrastructure so the tool is usable by a broader audience.

## Roadmap & Delivery Plan
Planned steps include hiring a developer and a designer to build a smoother public interface; polishing usability; and layering in infrastructure for scale. The team references a January beta target and says cushion time has been built into the schedule. As part of this plan, the team proposes to tailor the initial beta interface and user experience specifically for the needs and workflows of the proposed target segment of digital illustrators. To inform this tailoring, the team proposes a small-scale, planned test with a handful of digital illustrators from the target platform to gather initial workflow feedback before the beta, planned for the month following successful funding. This test is proposed to involve a clear, simple metric of 5 test users to show structured planning and manageability. A proposed, clear metric for the success of this test is the percentage of test users who successfully completed the fingerprinting workflow without assistance. Furthermore, the team proposes a planned, small-scale public demonstration of the technology's verification capability using a sample file to be conducted during the crowdfunding campaign to build trust, planned for the third week of the campaign. To help visualize the solution for this segment, the team proposes to include a mock-up or wireframe screenshot of the proposed beta interface tailored for digital illustrators in the project description.

## Revenue Model and Sustainability
To address a key backer question about long-term viability, the team is considering a proposed, simple pricing structure. This could take the form of a freemium model, for example, offering a limited number of free verifications per month with a subscription option for higher-volume users. As a hypothetical example to make this tangible, a proposed pricing tier could be '5 free verifications per month, then $5 per month for unlimited.' The final model would be developed based on feedback from the initial beta and the proposed small-scale test.

## Why Crowdfunding / Use of Funds
Funds will support building a public-facing site and the underlying infrastructure, along with the hiring needed to deliver a refined interface and broaden access. This includes proposed work to adapt the initial product for the specific segment, to conduct the proposed small-scale test, to execute the proposed public demonstration, and to create the proposed interface mock-up or wireframe.

## Risks & Challenges
The main risk is talent acquisition: delays in hiring or extended timelines could push back the January beta. Mitigations include existing architecture, a lean scope, added schedule buffer, and a commitment to communicate changes clearly. Focusing on a narrow initial segment is a proposed strategy to manage scope and accelerate learning.

## Team & Partnerships
The effort is led by engineers who emphasize building for everyday creators in their lives. All architecture and content are created and reviewed by a human team.

## Technical Details
Only hashed fingerprints are stored, dramatically reducing storage and compute compared with systems that store full files or rely on energy-intensive consensus mechanisms. The goal is long-term security and transparency with minimal environmental impact. To enhance credibility and transparency, the team proposes to anchor fingerprints to a specific public ledger technology, such as a public timestamping service like OpenTimestamps or a specific, energy-efficient blockchain.

## Support & Post-Launch Plans
The team promises clear communication with backers if plans change and notes limited, supportive use of AI tools for coding and documentation; they are not building AI technology nor using AI to generate creative assets. The plan is to gather feedback from the initial, focused user segment, informed by the proposed small-scale test, to inform broader development and the proposed pricing model.
